newsitem.title: Turkmenistan: Turkmenistan grain harvest net 400,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan grain harvest net 400,000 T.

text.p: Turkmenistan's 1996 grain harvest totalled a net 400,000 tonnes, far below last year's 1.0 million tonnes and way below an even higher government target of 1.2 million tonnes, state television said on Tuesday.

President Saparmurat Niyazov, quoting the figures on a televised broadcast, said, "Turkmenistan has never worked so badly. We have no further choice -- either we starve or we fulfil the self-sufficiency programme."
Niyazov said grain and flour imports had cost the former Soviet republic around $800 million so far this year.
He gave no details of where the grain and flour were bought, but industry sources have said the main suppliers were Kazakhstan and Ukraine.
State television said 20 percent of livestock in Turkmenistan, which borders Iran on the eastern edge of the Caspian Sea, had died in 1996 for lack of feed grains.
Niyazov, the republic's former Communist Party boss, has continued with state-led economic policies similar to those of his Soviet past.
But state subsidies have not prevented serious food shortages for 3.8 million people who require around 1.5 million tonnes of grain annually.
Annual demand for feed grain was not immediately available.
Earlier this month, the Turkmen government doubled the state price for a loaf of bread to 400 manats, while a loaf of traditional flat bread now sells in private markets for around 1,500 manats.
